title: Introduction to ArchiMate Notation
explanation: ArchiMate is an open and independent modelling language for enterprise architecture. It provides a uniform representation for diagrams that describe enterprise architectures across business, application, and technology layers. This module introduces the core concepts and notation conventions used in ArchiMate diagrams.

annotations.explanation: The top layer shows business actors, processes, and services that deliver value to customers.
The middle layer shows application components and services that support business processes.
The bottom layer shows infrastructure nodes, devices, and networks that host applications.

walkthrough.instruction: Start by identifying the business services your architecture supports. Place Business Service elements at the top of your diagram.
Add Application Components that realise the business services. Connect them using Realisation relationships.
Add Technology Nodes that host the application components. Use Assignment relationships to show deployment.

exercises.scenario: A government digital service allows citizens to apply for a licence online. The service uses a web application hosted on cloud infrastructure with a database backend. Model this using ArchiMate layers.
hints: Start with the Business Service: 'Licence Application'
Add an Application Component for the web app and a Data Object for the application form
Include Technology Nodes for the cloud hosting and database server

commonMistakes.description: Mixing elements from different layers without proper cross-layer relationships
commonMistakes.incorrectExample: Placing a Node directly inside a Business Process without a Realisation or Serving relationship
commonMistakes.correctedExample: Use Serving relationships to connect Technology Services to Application Components, and Realisation relationships from Application Services to Business Services
commonMistakes.explanation: ArchiMate layers should be connected through well-defined cross-layer relationships. Direct containment across layers violates the metamodel and makes diagrams harder to understand.
